findings.title: Task 6's unconditional registration breaks an existing registry-invariant test; no task updates it
findings.description: `test_exactly_the_three_builtin_tools_are_registered` asserts `set(tools.list_tools()) == {"read_file", "write_file", "bash"}` and `test_materialize_binds_every_registered_tool` asserts `len(executors) == 3`. Task 6.4 registers five `cf_*` tools at package import via the side-effect line in `src/squadron/tools/__init__.py`, so both assertions fail the moment Task 6 lands — contradicting the file's own Sequencing claim that "Each task leaves the suite green," and Task 6's success criteria don't name the fix. A junior implementer at Task 6 hits a red test in an unrelated module with no instruction. No task in 1–9 mentions editing `tests/tools/test_package.py`. Add that edit to Task 6 (and note the `__init__.py` docstring claim "registers the built-in tools and does nothing else" also becomes stale), or the plan should state the new invariant once (builtins ∪ cf_* read from `list_tools()`) so the two assertions follow.

findings.title: The "non-text blocks are noted by type" mapping rule is implemented but has no test
findings.description: The design lists four Result mapping rules (`264-slice...:132-137`), and Task 4.2 implements all four including "Non-text blocks noted by type in the content." Success criterion 2 requires results be mapped "per the Result mapping rules," but the Task 3 fake server exposes only `echo`, `fail`, `sleep`, `empty` (task file:105-111) — every block it can return is text. Task 5.1 therefore tests join, `isError`, and zero-content, and nothing can exercise the non-text branch; it ships untested. Requirement left unmet: a non-text `CallToolResult` must surface its block type rather than being dropped. Fix cheaply — add one fake-server tool that returns an `ImageContent`/non-text block and one assertion in Task 5.1.

findings.title: Success criterion 6 is only half scheduled; the slice merges with its second half unmet
findings.description: SC6 (`264-slice...:229-231`) requires two things: the materialized `cf_workflow_status` executor returning real project status, **and** a dispatch with a tool-capable non-SDK model calling `cf_build_context` and receiving assembled context (walkthrough §4). Task 9.1 covers the first (step 2); 9.3 mentions step 4 in prose as "remains open alongside 263's demo," and Task 9's success criteria gate on "walkthrough steps 1–3 recorded" before 9.4 merges the branch. So the plan's close-out criteria permit merging while a named success criterion is unverified, with the deferral recorded only inside a docs sub-bullet rather than as an explicit open checklist item. Either add step 4 as its own unchecked task item (carried as an open item with an owner) or amend the slice design to move it out of SC6. The `CLAUDECODE`-guard justification is legitimate; the tracking form is not.

findings.title: Task 8's availability rationale contradicts this repo's CI, and the `network` marker is unhandled
findings.description: Task 8 justifies the gate as "CI without node stays green, any environment with CF verifies the contract" (task file:255-260). This project's CI does the opposite: it installs `setup-node@v4` with node 22, runs `npm i -g @context-forge/cli` and `cf init --lite --no-ide`, then `uv run pytest` (ci.yml:20-24, 32). So the live contract test will actually run in CI against `cf.mcp_command`'s default `npx -y @context-forge/mcp`, which the design's own Risks section says downloads the package on first call. Consequence: the plan's determinism assumption for CI is wrong, and `pyproject.toml:83-85` already declares a `network` marker that Task 8 does not mention applying. Task 8 should state the real CI behavior and choose one: mark the module `network`, or have CI pin `cf.mcp_command` to a pre-fetched/pinned launch. (CI gating itself is not implicit — it is already wired by the existing `uv run pytest` step, so no extra gating task is required.)

findings.title: Proportionality: 9 tasks / 9 mandated commits for a 2/5-effort, two-module slice
findings.description: Effort is self-scored 2/5 for two new source modules (~80 + ~150 lines) and four test files, yet the breakdown spends a full task and a full commit on adding two `CONFIG_KEYS` dict entries (Task 1, effort 1/5) plus two assertions in an existing test class (Task 2, effort 1/5). The design's Files-changed table lists eight paths; the plan needs roughly half this task count. Merge Task 1+2 into one task (they are one commit point by the test-with pattern anyway — splitting them forces an untested commit at Task 1), and fold Task 3's fixture into the Task 4/5 bridge pair so the commit cadence lands on genuinely tested points rather than one commit per task. The per-task `ruff format` + commit lines are also encoded as checklist items (`- [ ]`) inside success criteria; commit markers belong as plain lines at working/tested points, not as a nine-item checkbox column.

findings.title: Task 3's stated justification is wrong for the tasks it names
findings.description: "tasks 5, 6 both need a real stdio peer" — Task 6 (`cf_tools.py`) delegates to `call_mcp_tool`, and Task 7's success criterion explicitly requires "green with no network and no node" via a mocked transport; Task 8 uses the real CF server, not the fake one. Only Task 5 needs the fixture. Ordering is harmless; the rationale should say so to stop a junior from wiring descriptors against the fake server.

findings.title: Task 5.2's process-reaping assertion offers one path that needs an unavailable dependency
findings.description: "scan for the fixture's command line" requires a process-listing facility; `psutil` is not in `pyproject.toml` dependencies or dev groups. The PID-temp-file alternative works with stdlib (`os.kill(pid, 0)`), but the plan should name that as the approach and say how the fake server learns the path (env var or argv), since Task 3.1 currently describes no such hook.

findings.title: Execute-time config reads put TOML file I/O inside an async turn
findings.description: Task 6.3 reads `cf.mcp_command`/`cf.mcp_timeout_s` at execute time, which is deliberate (it keeps `sq config set` effective without re-materializing, and Task 7.3 tests it). It does, however, sit against the convention documented in the openai provider — "no config file I/O happens inside an async turn" — for these tools' loop bounds. Given the same call already spawns a subprocess and runs `initialize()`, two small TOML reads are noise; recording why this is the accepted exception in the module comment would keep the rule from looking inconsistently applied.
